root_cause: A list of five slowest individual GitHub jobs lacks recurrence and independent-attempt evidence, so promoting a one-off job as an autonomous optimization priority is unwarranted.

observed_evidence.interpretation: one-off maximum is not a repeated bottleneck or a before/after speedup

failed_approaches: Automatically prioritize one outlying slow job
Use truncated/partial provider jobs as if verified
Create another recurring metrics agent or CI workflow
Claim SLO or faster build from one Janitor measurement
fix: Derive bounded, read-only per-job repeated evidence from existing Janitor telemetry; require >=20 valid executed jobs from >=5 attempts overall, >=3 independent attempts of same workflow/job signature, and >=60s sample median execution time before exposing a suggested specialist lane; otherwise no priority. Retain raw IDs, SHAs, p95 and no-dispatch flags.
prevention_rule: Only the original domain/PR owner may investigate or implement based on the advisory after checking canonical Brain skills, source/owner lineage and true before/after baselines. Never dispatch or mutate from this diagnostic, skip Required/CodeQL or change required gates; unknown lane stays unassigned. Existing hourly Janitor only, one canonical incident #4661 and skill projection.

invariants: no action from a single outlier
at least 20 complete job rows and 5 separate run attempts
at least 3 recurring job attempts and 60000ms median for candidate priority
all sample identities, status and durations independently validated
any incomplete or inconsistent telemetry suppresses all priorities
never dispatch a workflow or auto-promote
same hourly Janitor schedule and artifact evidence only

terminal_rule: Protected Required, CodeQL, main readback, Brain skill projection and a subsequent existing Janitor execution at merged main SHA must be observed before claiming runtime live. The advisory is not proof of speedup, autonomous repair or portal business impact.
